{{short description|American basketball player (born 2002)}} {{about|the basketball player|other people|Mike Miles (disambiguation){{!}}Mike Miles}} {{Use mdy dates|date=November 2023}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Mike Miles | image = Mike Miles.jpg | caption = Miles with [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] in 2021 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2002|8|24}} | birth_place = [[Highland Hills, Dallas]], [[Texas]], U.S.A. | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 2 | weight_lbs = 220 | league = [[Baloncesto Profesional Colombiano]] | team = Paisas | position = [[Point guard]] / [[Shooting guard]] | number = 3 | high_school = [[Lancaster High School (Lancaster, Texas)|Lancaster]]
([[Lancaster, Texas]]) | college = [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] (2020–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | career_start = 2023 | career_end = | years1 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team1 = [[Texas Legends]] | years2 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = [[Iowa Wolves]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]]–[[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]] | team3 = [[Windy City Bulls]] | years4 = 2026–present | team4 = [[Paisas Basketball|Paisas de Medellín]] | highlights = * 2× Second-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2022, 2023) * Big 12 All-Freshman Team (2021) | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalGold|[[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 Latvia]]|[[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|Team]]}} }} '''Michael Derrell Miles Jr.''' (born August 24, 2002) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Paisas Basketball|Paisas de Medellín]] of the [[Baloncesto Profesional Colombiano]]. He played [[college basketball]] at [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]]. ==Early life and high school career== Miles grew up playing basketball for the Texas Titans on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit alongside [[Cade Cunningham]].{{cite web |last1=Unruh |first1=Jacob |title=OSU basketball: Cade Cunningham faces unique challenge this week — his close friends |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/columns/2020/12/16/osu-basketball-cade-cunningham-faces-unique-challenge-this-week-his-close-friends/316893007/ |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |access-date=June 4, 2021 |date=December 15, 2021}} When Miles was in fourth grade, his AAU highlight videos drew national attention; [[Yahoo Sports]] labeled him "the elementary school [[Allen Iverson]]."{{cite web |last1=Nicholson |first1=Eric |title=Meet DISD's Other Mike Miles, The 9-Year-Old Basketball Prodigy |url=https://www.dallasobserver.com/news/meet-disds-other-mike-miles-the-9-year-old-basketball-prodigy-7137516 |website=[[Dallas Observer]] |access-date=June 4, 2021 |date=July 6, 2012}}{{cite web |title=Meet Mike Miles, the elementary school Allen Iverson |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/highschool-prep-rally/meet-mike-miles-elementary-school-allen-iverson-130304549.html |website=[[Yahoo Sports]] |access-date=June 4, 2021 |date=July 5, 2012}} He attended [[Lancaster High School (Lancaster, Texas)|Lancaster High School]] in [[Lancaster, Texas]].{{cite web |last1=Riddle |first1=Greg |title=Lancaster's Mike Miles, the Dallas area's No. 2-ranked basketball recruit, commits to TCU |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2019/12/22/lancasters-mike-miles-the-dallas-areas-no-2-ranked-basketball-recruit-commits-to-tcu/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=June 4, 2021 |date=December 22, 2019}} As a junior, he averaged 18 points, 4.5 assists and 2.3 steals per game, leading his team to a 31–3 record. As a senior, Miles averaged 21.4 points, four rebounds, four assists and three steals per game, leading his team to a 36–1 record. He was named SportsDayHS All-Area Player of the Year by ''[[The Dallas Morning News]]'', as well as Class 5A Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Hoyt |first1=Joseph |title=2020 SportsDayHS boys basketball Player of the Year: Lancaster's Mike Miles |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2020/03/27/2020-sportsdayhs-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year-lancasters-mike-miles/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=June 4, 2021 |date=March 27, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Jeremy |title=TCU basketball signee Mike Miles named TABC Class 5A POY |url=https://247sports.com/college/tcu/Article/TCU-signee-Mike-Miles-named-player-of-year-146804285/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=June 4, 2021 |date=May 4, 2020}} Miles committed to playing college basketball for [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] over offers from [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]], [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], among other programs.{{cite web |last1=Davison |first1=Drew |title=TCU basketball lands much-needed point guard for 2020 class |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article238644568.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=June 4, 2021 |date=December 22, 2019}} ==College career== On January 30, 2021, Miles recorded a freshman season-high 28 points and five assists in a 102–98 overtime loss to [[Missouri Tigers men's basketball|Missouri]].{{cite web |last1=Davison |first1=Drew |title=TCU basketball can't close out No. 12 Missouri as Tigers rally for overtime victory |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article248795525.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=June 4, 2021 |date=January 30, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 13.6 points, 3.5 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. Miles was named to the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team and earned All-Big 12 honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Davison |first1=Drew |title=TCU's Mike Miles invited to USA Basketball's U19 training camp in Fort Worth next month |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article251212679.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=June 4, 2021 |date=May 7, 2021}} As a sophomore, he averaged 15.4 points, 3.8 assists and 3.5 rebounds per game. He was named to the Second Team All-Big 12 as a sophomore.{{cite news |last1=Howard |first1=Nicholas |title=TCU Men's Basketball: Frogs Look to Go Far in Big 12 Tournament |url=https://www.si.com/college/tcu/basketball/tcu-mbb-preview-vs-texas-big12-tourney |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 9, 2022}} On March 30, 2022, Miles declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{Cite web |last=Hodges |first=Russell |date=March 30, 2022 |title=TCU guard Mike Miles declares for the NBA Draft |url=https://www.frogsowar.com/2022/3/30/23003499/tcu-guard-mike-miles-declares-for-the-nba-draft |access-date=March 30, 2022 |website=Frogs O' War |language=en}} However, he later clarified that he did not hire an agent and is maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Davison |first1=Drew |title=NBA hopeful Mike Miles opens door on possible return to TCU basketball |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article260258725.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=April 8, 2022 |date=April 8, 2022}} On April 11, Miles withdrew from the draft and announced he would return to TCU for his junior season.{{cite web |last1=Davison |first1=Drew |title=Change of heart: Mike Miles returning to TCU basketball for 'unfinished business' |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/college/big-12/texas-christian-university/article260329360.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=April 11, 2022 |date=April 11, 2022}} He was named to the Second Team All-Big 12 as a junior.{{cite web |last1=North |first1=Anthony |title=Three Horned Frogs named to Big 12 Basketball All-Conference teams |url=https://www.frogsowar.com/2023/3/5/23626456/three-horned-frogs-named-to-big-12-basketball-all-conference-teams |website=Frogs o' War |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=March 6, 2023 |date=March 5, 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Texas Legends (2023–2024)=== After going undrafted in the [[2023 NBA draft]], Miles signed a two-way contract with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Mavericks have signed Mike Miles Jr. to a Two-Way contract.|number=1680043407174139904|user=MavsPR|date=July 14, 2023|access-date=July 14, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 14.{{cite tweet|author=Mavs PR|title=The Dallas Mavericks announced today that they have waived guard Mike Miles Jr., guard Jordan Walker and guard/forward Joe Wieskamp.|number=1713251311309795778|user=MavsPR|date=October 14, 2023|access-date=October 15, 2023}} On October 29, he joined the [[Texas Legends]].{{cite web|first=Britney|last=Wynn|title=LEGENDS DRAFT FOUR, FINALIZE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER|url=https://texas.gleague.nba.com/news/legends-draft-four-finalize-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=December 14, 2023}} On July 26, 2024, Miles signed with Greek club [[Aris B.C.|Aris Midea]],{{cite web|title=Ο Mike Miles JR στον ΑΡΗ Midea|url=https://www.arisbc.gr/el/enimerosi/eidiseis/o-mike-miles-jr-ston-ari-midea.html|website=ArisBC.gr|date=July 26, 2024|access-date=July 26, 2024|language=Greek}} but parted ways with the team, citing personal reasons in August. ===Iowa Wolves (2024)=== On October 25, 2024, Miles joined the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Iowa Wolves Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Iowa-Wolves/4/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=November 11, 2024}} However, he was waived on December 13.{{cite web|title=Wolves Add Will Baker; Waive Mike Miles Jr.|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-add-will-baker-waive-mike-miles-jr|website=NBA.com|date=December 13, 2024|access-date=December 14, 2024}} ===Windy City Bulls (2024–2026)=== On December 27, 2024, Miles joined the [[Windy City Bulls]].{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Windy City Bulls Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Windy-City-Bulls/44/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 28, 2024}} ==National team career== Miles represented the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2021 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2021 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]] in Latvia. He averaged 9.1 points, 3.9 assists and 3.3 rebounds per game, helping his team win the gold medal.{{cite web |last1=Riddle |first1=Greg |title=Former Lancaster star Mike Miles, former St. Mark’s star Harrison Ingram help U.S. win U19 World Cup |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2021/07/11/former-lancaster-star-mike-miles-former-st-marks-star-harrison-ingram-help-us-win-u19-world-cup/ |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=July 12, 2021 |date=July 11, 2021}} ==Personal life== Miles is the son of Jeanee Miles.{{cite web |title=Mike Miles Jr. - Men's Basketball |url=https://gofrogs.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/mike-miles-jr-/14500 |website=TCU Athletics |access-date=29 July 2024 |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}}
